answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The atlas multiplier is published, charged in signal, and ripple lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1223 identities would post 1143 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
